records.summary: The look of a control is its appearance; type named it before the axes were split.
sf-alert's look is its appearance, not a variant.
What an alert or a toast reports is its status; type answered that question before the axes were split.
A progress indicator's colour role is its status.
What a component is made of is its kind.
records.manual: sf-tree-item also reads type from its item data (_sourceData.type); write kind there too.

records.summary: What a component is made of is its kind, not a variant.
sf-tag's type answered two questions: a kind (checkbox, icon, color, avatar, default) and a status (info, success, warning, error). Each now has its own axis.
records.manual: Write kind= when the value is checkbox, icon, color, avatar or default, and status= when it is info, success, warning or error.

records.summary: sf-badge's scheme carried statuses; status is the axis now.
records.manual: Move a status value (info, success, warning, error) from scheme= to status=; a colour scheme value stays where it is.

records.summary: Every field takes its size from one attribute, size.
Icon positions are logical, so they follow the writing direction.
Inner spacing is one profile, spacing, with named values.
records.manual: tightness=low becomes spacing=compact, default (or empty) becomes normal, high becomes comfortable, highest becomes spacious.

records.summary: size names the size ladder everywhere; a file's byte size is file-size.
Classes for the gallery's lightbox are lightbox-class; class and root-class belong to the element itself.
The scrollbar's mode is data-mode.
One word for a failure across the Framework: error.
The status without a meaning is neutral; components had their own words for it.
A file preview that picks its look by itself is auto.
A tag with a count is a default tag with count=.
records.manual: Keep the number in count=.

records.summary: The drawer is on the shared size ladder.
Placement is logical, so a drawer follows the writing direction.
records.manual: Only where the page may be right-to-left does the difference show: left stays on the left there, inline-start moves to the right.

records.summary: Context menu positions name a side and an edge in one vocabulary.
Form fields have three sizes: 1/2, 1 and 2.
A committed value change is change on every form value control.
records.manual: sf-range-slider-change also fired when a value was set from code; change does not. Code that relied on the event after a programmatic set calls its handler itself.

records.summary: Modal lifecycle events are modal:*.
A modal created through the loader is listened to with modal:* events, not callback options.
records.manual: Replace the option with an addEventListener call for the event named in to.

records.summary: The loader's standAlone flag is accepted and ignored.
records.manual: Delete the option; it has no effect.

records.summary: A button without fill or border is the link appearance.
The scrollbar's class carries the sf- prefix like every component class.
hide-show no longer writes hidden, hidden>block and block>hidden; it still reads and removes them.
records.manual: Remove these classes from markup; hide-show manages visibility itself.

records.summary: Side utilities are logical: inline-start and inline-end.
Gap utilities live in the gap module.
The text-a0 … text-i9 classes set font size and line height equal to raw primitives, which is no type pair; nobody used them.
records.manual: Use the text scale classes, which pair a size with its line height.

records.summary: Two names for one radius; rounded stays.
The radius names its role now: --sf-radius--ui for a control, --sf-radius--surface for a block.
records.manual: A control takes --sf-radius--ui (4px); a large block takes --sf-radius--surface (8px), which is not what the old 4px gave it. In the same pair as the removal: the ui-doc guide page design-tokens/index.md (section «Радиусы») drops the old name, and the generated design-tokens/all-tokens.md is regenerated with scripts/build-token-reference.mjs, or docs:check goes red in between.

records.summary: sf-toggle and sf-switch drew one control; the switch carries both looks now.
records.manual: Sizes do not map one to one: toggle size 1 was a 40×20 track, the switch is 48×24 at size 1 on desktop. sf-switch--short and sf-switch--icon give the toggle's two looks.

records.summary: Components keep the old JS property names next to the new ones.

items.to: el.appearance, el.kind or el.status (as the attribute)

records.manual: Read the property named after the attribute's new name.

records.summary: A field's filter renderer is chosen by its property type. Eight control names the table used before, read at field.filter.control, are kept as aliases; field.type and field.dataType are older names for propertyType.
records.manual: Declare propertyType on the field instead of filter.control, type or dataType; the renderer is the same. The eight control names: range, date-range, multi-select, single-select, choice, choices, entity-multi-select, entity-single-select.

records.summary: The not-placed bin is the Framework's accordion now, with no hint line under its heading: the sentence described what the «+» beside every area does, under a heading that already says what the bin is. The attribute still parses and still does nothing.
records.manual: Remove the attribute from the tag. Nothing replaces it: the bin's heading says what the bin is, and the «+» beside every area is what offers a field back, which is what the sentence described.

records.summary: The text-size steps 1/7, 1/6 and 1/5 leave the public scale: they have no line height and no text role, so no text can be set in them. The smallest public step is 1/4.
records.manual: Set text in a role (body, label, caption) or in step 1/4 or larger. A skeleton line takes the size of the text it stands in for: use the same step that text uses, never a step below 1/4.

records.summary: sf-table, sf-data-view, sf-property-view and sf-admin-menu left the free Framework for the SIMAI Framework Pro package. They are not deprecated: the tags, attributes, events and ports are unchanged, but a free release no longer carries them, so a page that uses them and declares no Pro package renders nothing for those tags.
records.manual: Declare the Pro package before core.js loads: SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.pro = {base: '<ui-pro>/smart'}, where <ui-pro> is where the page serves simai/ui-pro (its smart/ directory is the package base and smart/rule.js its rule file). Pin a Pro release whose lock (simai/ui-pro contracts/releases/pro-<12>.lock.json) names, in requires.framework, the free release the page pins (ui-<12>), and serve both from those releases; ui-09bc6b371eca is the first free release without the four components, pro-1f894a46f488 the Pro release built against it. Change nothing in the markup. The record is removed, not compat, because there is no alias to sweep: the free release dropped the components at once, and the Pro package carries them unchanged. deprecated_on and remove_after are the policy's dates for the day of the move and mean nothing further here. sf-upgrade reports a use of the four tags only in a project that declares no Pro package. The package is under the SIMAI Framework Pro licence, whose terms are pending (see the source).

records.summary: sf-table, sf-data-view, sf-property-view and sf-admin-menu moved from the SIMAI Framework Pro package to the larena package: SIMAI Framework Pro is dropped and a component lives with its owner. The tags, attributes, events and ports are unchanged; what a page declares changes from packages.pro to packages.larena.
records.manual: Declare the larena package instead of pro, before core.js loads: SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.larena = {base: '<package base>'}, where the base is the smart/ directory of a larena package build (its smart/rule.js registers the package). Use a build whose receipt (package-receipt.json) names, as its framework release, the free release the page pins. Change nothing in the markup. The record is removed, not compat: package pro is no longer published, so there is no alias to sweep.

records.summary: Status classes take the status vocabulary: error, neutral, info. The older colour names still draw the same.
The spacing classes of a button follow its spacing attribute; the tightness classes are its older names.
The role a popover gives its surface is surface-role; a role attribute on the host made the host itself a menu or dialog beside the surface.
The modal root's position class is sf-modal--position-*; the misspelt sf-modal--positon-* is still written beside it as a legacy alias.
The Smart button's ghost appearance is the link appearance under its old name, as the class sf-button--ghost already is.
records.manual: appearance="ghost" becomes appearance="link".

records.summary: --sf-heading--font-family, --sf-heading--font-weight and --sf-heading--font-style are read by no rule: headings (h1-h6 and .sf-h-1 to .sf-h-6) take their face and weight from --sf-heading--family and --sf-heading--weight, and display text (.sf-display-1 to .sf-display-6) from --sf-display--family and --sf-display--weight. They stay defined until remove_after and then leave.
records.manual: Set a heading's face with --sf-heading--family and its weight with --sf-heading--weight (--sf-display--family and --sf-display--weight for .sf-display-*), or a class on the heading. The record named a title role sf-title-* that does not exist (documentation trial 6, 2026-10-18).

records.summary: A data format names itself without a version: "schema": "simai.<name>" with "schema_version": <major>, an integer, beside it, in place of the older "schema": "simai.<name>.v<major>". Every Framework reader takes both forms until remove_after; the Framework's writers move to the new form in the next release, and sf-upgrade rewrites a project's declarations (rewrite rename-format; an item marked held stays as it is). As of 2026-10-18 the Framework's writers emit the new form (the Composition builtins, field kinds, type and port registries, capability fixtures, the technology packet, a Document and its dependency receipt resolved from a recipe named without a version) and its own data files carry it; the editor manifest registry followed once Larena's backend read both forms (larena b7b751891). Left in the older form on purpose, each read by that label or pinned by digest outside ui-source: simai.smart-component-contract-registry.v2 (ui-studio, frozen, reads it by this label), simai.composite.host-port.v1 and simai.composite.host-port.conformance.v1 (published port editions and kits, pinned by digest), simai.composition.capability-contract-lock.v1 and simai.composition.recipe-contract-lock.v1 (ui-builder packages the normative files by them), the files of the Recipe contract with simai.composition.recipe-limits.v1 and simai.recipe.canonicalization-vectors.v1 (a published contract whose lock pins their bytes; since Recipe 1.1.0, 2026-10-19, its schemas take simai.composition.recipe, recipe-manifest, inputs and dependencies and the profile simai.recipe.canonical-json in either form, so those four are no longer held; a recipe in the older form still resolves to a simai.composition.document.v1 Document and a simai.composition.dependencies.v1 receipt with the digests its 1.0.1 fixture fixes), simai.smart-component-fixture.v2, simai.smart-component-scenario.v1 and simai.smart.sources-local-map.v1 (ui-studio validates them by const), and the frozen copies under contracts/standards.

a recipe's form decides the Document and digests it resolves to; sf-upgrade leaves stored recipes as they are, and their owner moves them (the Recipe contract 1.1.0 accepts both forms)

records.manual: sf-upgrade --apply rewrites a declaration of a format: in a JSON file that keeps the standard layout (JSON.stringify with two or four spaces, or tabs), every "schema": "simai.<name>.v<major>" becomes "schema": "simai.<name>" with "schema_version": <major> right after it; in a script, a literal schema: 'simai.<name>.v<major>' (or 'schema' => '...' in PHP) gains schema_version beside it when the file names schema_version nowhere else. What it reports and leaves: a comparison against the label (a reader of your own: read both forms until remove_after with readSchema or isSchema from core/js/composition/schema-name.mjs), a JSON file in another layout, and every format an item marks held -- the Framework itself keeps those in the older form for the reason given, so leave them until the item is released.

records.summary: sf-theme-generator's events are sf-theme-generator-change and sf-theme-generator-apply; their first names, sf-theme-change and sf-theme-apply, clash with the Loader's light/dark event and are emitted beside them until the sweep.

The runtime's own names on window.SF -- the message bus, the runtime module registry's own state, the Smart base's announcement and litHtml -- live under SF.__internal; the old names read and write through to it, noted as deprecated, until the sweep. SF.loadSmartBase, SF.smart, SF.smartBaseReady, SF.loadRuntime and SF.runtimeModule are public and stay.
records.manual: Nothing a page needs is here: use the public API (core/contracts/public-js-api.json). Code of the Framework's own reads SF.__internal.<name>.

records.summary: A box that holds its own overlays is marked data-sf-overlay-container, one name for sf-drawer and sf-modal; data-sf-drawer-container, the drawer's name of the same day, is read until remove_after.
records.manual: Rename the attribute on the box (and any selector that names it) to data-sf-overlay-container.

records.summary: A composition value type is named without a version: record-changed, record-removed, collection-changed, files-moved, counter, navigation, preference-changed, record-id, record-ids, text and boolean, in place of the older labels record-changed.v1 and the rest. The Framework reads both forms everywhere it reads a value type until remove_after: a page effect's type in a port answer (sf-page-host, SF.Composition.publishEffects), a port manifest, a fragment descriptor, a declared or rendered route and an element's static sfPorts; a route joins a bare name and its older label as one type. The published schemas take both (composition-port-manifest.v1.schema.json, the fragment descriptor schema 1.2.0), the port registry composition-ports.v1.json keeps the older labels as its value_types keys and maps each bare name to its key in value_type_names, and the routing contract 1.1.0 records both forms in fixtures/value-type-names.json. Left in the older form on purpose until remove_after, so published bytes and digests do not move: VALUE_TYPES keys, the built-in sf-table port manifest (pinned in the routing contract lock), the outputs sf-page-host declares, and fixtures/routing.json.
records.manual: Name each value type without its version: in a host's port answers (effects[].type), port manifests (outputs/inputs value), fragment descriptors, an element's static sfPorts and a page's data-sf-routes. Both forms are read until remove_after, so a host, a component and a page may move one at a time; a route between a bare name and its older label already works.

records.summary: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA held the older label of the effect format, simai.effect.v1, and was described as the label a writer emits, against format-names-without-version. A writer now spreads SF.Effects.EFFECT_FORMAT, {schema: 'simai.effect', schema_version: 1}, into an effect.json. EFFECT_SCHEMA keeps its value until remove_after, so a writer that put it alone in "schema" still writes a manifest every reader takes; reading it through SF.Effects is noted in SF.deprecations. Readers take both forms of the format name either way.
records.manual: Where code writes {schema: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA, ...} (or imports EFFECT_SCHEMA from core/js/effects.js), write {...SF.Effects.EFFECT_FORMAT, ...}. A comparison against the label is a reader: use isSchema(manifest, 'simai.effect', 1) from core/js/composition/schema-name.mjs, or SF.Effects.checkEffectManifest.

records.summary: The size ladder decides a spinner's geometry (simai/ui-source#10): at each step, 1/3 to 3, its diameter is the icon of an sf-button of the same size and its stroke that icon's stroke. The pixel attributes that let a page draw its own spinner -- data-width (and data-w), data-height (data-h), data-stroke-width and data-dot-radius on .sf-loader-container, and width, height, stroke-width and dot-radius on sf-spinner, which write them -- are still read until remove_after: a spinner given any of them is drawn in pixels as before, and each is noted in SF.deprecations.
records.manual: Remove the pixel attributes and pick the step whose icon the spinner stands beside or in place of: size="1/3|1/2|1|2|3" on sf-spinner, the class sf-loader--size-<step> on .sf-loader-container (step 1 when none is written). The stroke comes with the step. The colour is the current ink; set --sf-loader--color on the spinner or an ancestor to give it another.

records.summary: A loading button shows the spinner at its icon's size (simai/ui-source#10) -- sf-button, sf-icon-button and the buttons of sf-button-group, the segmented one included -- and the moving stripes are no longer the loading look. The Framework no longer sets --sf-button-loading-stripe or --sf-icon-button-loading-stripe; a page that sets either still gets still stripes in that colour over a loading button until remove_after, and nothing when it is unset.
records.manual: Delete the variable: a loading button shows the spinner, in the button's ink. To colour the spinner, set --sf-loader--color on the button or an ancestor.

records.summary: sf-input is served from smart/input/ since its folder took the tag's name (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8 §3, §21): js/input.js and css/input.css, loader bundle cl-input. The old path keeps working until remove_after: smart/inputs/js/inputs.js is a forwarding script that notes the path in SF.deprecations and loads smart/input/js/input.js, smart/inputs/css/inputs.css is sf-input's sheet, the Loader forwards the bundle name cl-inputs to cl-input (src/core/contracts/smart-rule-forwards.v1.json), and the registry id smart.inputs is a dated alias of smart.input, the id that follows the folder and the tag.
records.manual: Write smart/input/ for smart/inputs/ and input for inputs in the file names (js/input.js, js/input.min.js, css/input.css, css/input.min.css); in a product rule's relation write cl-input for cl-inputs, and in a manifest or a package contract smart.input for smart.inputs. A page that lets the Loader fetch sf-input needs no change.
